stops.note: from 'býr', village or farmstead, the same element found in English place-names ending in -by like Whitby and Derby
used in the Danelaw for local rules set by a township
the 'by' was later reinterpreted as 'secondary' or 'side', shaping the modern sense of a subsidiary rule
stops.meaning: a rule made by a local body or organization

current_meaning: a rule made by a local authority or an organization for its own members
